verdict.rationale: Next.js is itself the full-stack React meta-framework the story describes. The docs cover file-system routing with layouts and advanced patterns, async server components that await data, server functions, API endpoints, and per-page rendering and caching. Community users who built production apps confirm the routing and data features ("batteries included", filesystem routing, SSR out of the box). missing for 10: the docs present it as a React framework rather than spelling out a separate official layer on top of a base framework, and community reports of undocumented behaviors leave some depth of the data-fetching docs uncorroborated.

support.subject: As a developer, I can use an official full-stack meta-framework built on top of the framework for routing and data fetching

citations.quote: Next.js is a React framework for building full-stack web applications.
Create routes using the file system, including support for more advanced routing patterns and UI layouts.
Make your React component async and await your data.
Run server code by calling a function. Skip the API.
the closest thing in JS to Rails/Phoenix 'batteries included.'
